newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat mostly lower, barley futures unchanged.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat mostly lower, barley futures unchanged.

text.p: UK wheat futures closed mostly lower on Thursday after failing to sustain early gains.
The market opened higher following Wednesday's news that the EU had scrapped the export duty on soft wheat, but prices drifted off as the bids at the weekly tender were released.
"People were expecting a lot more than 379,250 tonnes of soft wheat to be bid for," said a trader.
However, news that the EU had granted licences to export 237,470 tonnes of soft wheat at 4.97 ecu refund was within market expectation based on the figure bid for.
At the close prices were 0.20 stg down to unchanged on a turnover of 563 lots.
Nearby September, which goes off the board on Monday was one stg up.

Barley futures were unchanged on a turnover of 138 lots, with traders expecting the market to go lower following news that the EU had granted only licences to export 46,000 tonnes of free-market barley aganist bids for 94,000 tonnes.
"People were expecting more than this with the Saudi tender on Friday," said another trader.
Saudi Arabia is to tender for 1.72 million tonnes of any origin feed barley on September 20.
The EU sold 305,061 tonnes of German intervention barley at a minimum price of 103.15 ecus a tonne for export to non-EU countries.
"That looks like some of the Saudi business," said one trader.

When the Saudi tender was announced some UK traders thought the bulk would come from the EU with the British market picking up a fair size chunck...."because British barley is the cheapest at the moment," said a trader.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were neglected.
